scope: Six MiniMax-H3 windows and three stitched ten-second multitask robot drivers
summary: Corrected reference composition produced complete, sharp H3 robot-action windows for place-in-rack, unscrew-cap, and rinse-bottle, but their stitched subject seams remain too large for direct delivery and are routed only as Wan motion/geometry drivers.
evidence: All six independent H3 experiments completed on physical A800 GPUs 0, 2, and 3 with seed 20260811 and 20 steps.
Dense five-frame review of each window found coherent two-arm robot geometry, one persistent blue bottle, and task-specific motion; unscrewing visibly separates the cap.

All three stitched drivers decode to 240 frames at 24 FPS with SHA-256 values ed213c2faaf176670efe9462b2f51677d6a5a0164450b3769d11738e84204514, dc18ebc112f5f9e2be7836779653660d0657a48e23a6e32845b055a9b356b04b, and 10dfdd3226a9b4089fec3b3319327e78d32996caa83ef32517b28a105b9686e4.
Best overlap subject MAD remains 47.06 place, 41.09 unscrew, and 24.80 rinse, so direct H3 delivery is rejected.
lessons: Appending action-specific RGB continuation and control-video references preserves task state while retaining explicit motion conditioning.
Good individual windows do not waive a measured seam failure; the raw result can still serve as a second-stage driver.
limitations: The drivers use third-party H3 NF4 weights and hard seam selection; they are not final videos.
Action semantics remain camera-frame visual evidence, not force/contact or robot-base control.
next_actions: Use full-length robot-factored Wan replacement to regularize seams and enforce zero human residual without post blur.
